articles.title: Anthropic Releases Claude 4 with Extended Reasoning and 2M Token Context
articles.summary: Anthropic has unveiled Claude 4, its most capable model yet, featuring a 2 million token context window and enhanced chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. The model demonstrates significant improvements on coding and scientific benchmarks, outperforming competitors on several industry-standard tests. Claude 4 is available via API and through Claude.ai starting today.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2.5 Achieves Human-Level Performance on New Medical Licensing Exams
articles.summary: Google DeepMind announced that Gemini Ultra 2.5 has surpassed human expert performance on updated medical licensing examinations across six countries. The study, published in Nature Medicine, highlights the model's ability to synthesize complex clinical data and provide nuanced diagnostic reasoning. Researchers caution that real-world deployment still requires careful human oversight frameworks.

articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Operator Mode for Fully Autonomous Business Workflows
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced Operator Mode for GPT-5, enabling enterprises to deploy fully autonomous AI agents capable of managing multi-step business workflows without human intervention. The feature includes built-in audit trails and rollback mechanisms designed to satisfy corporate compliance requirements. Early enterprise customers including Salesforce and SAP are already piloting the system.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Agency Issues First Major Fines to Three Tech Firms
articles.summary: The newly operational EU AI Office has levied fines totaling €480 million against three unnamed technology companies for deploying high-risk AI systems without required conformity assessments. The enforcement actions are seen as a landmark test of the EU AI Act's teeth, drawing significant attention from global tech legal teams. Industry groups have called for clearer compliance guidelines ahead of further enforcement actions expected this summer.

articles.title: Meta Releases Llama 4 Scout Open-Source Model with Mixture-of-Experts Architecture
articles.summary: Meta has open-sourced Llama 4 Scout, a 120-billion parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates only 17 billion parameters per inference pass, dramatically reducing compute costs. The release includes fine-tuning recipes and quantized versions optimized for consumer-grade hardware. The model scores competitively with closed-source alternatives on major reasoning and instruction-following benchmarks.

articles.title: Microsoft and OpenAI Unveil Real-Time RAG Infrastructure for Enterprise Azure Deployments
articles.summary: Microsoft and OpenAI have jointly announced a new retrieval-augmented generation infrastructure layer for Azure AI Foundry that promises sub-100ms retrieval latency across datasets exceeding one billion documents. The system uses a novel hierarchical vector index combined with semantic caching to dramatically cut query costs. General availability is set for June 2026 with preview access opening this week.

articles.title: Stanford HAI Report Warns of Growing 'Alignment Tax' as Safety Measures Slow Model Deployment
articles.summary: Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute released its 2026 AI Index, highlighting what researchers are calling an 'alignment tax'—the measurable performance and speed costs associated with implementing safety guardrails in frontier models. The report finds that organizations under commercial pressure are increasingly opting for lighter safety interventions, raising concerns among policymakers. The authors recommend new funding mechanisms to make robust alignment research economically viable.

articles.title: Sora 2 Generates Fully Coherent 10-Minute Videos with Director-Mode Controls
articles.summary: OpenAI has quietly rolled out Sora 2 to select creative partners, featuring the ability to generate up to 10 minutes of temporally coherent video from text prompts. New director-mode controls allow users to specify camera movements, lighting conditions, and scene transitions using natural language commands. Film studios and advertising agencies have reportedly been testing the system under NDA for the past month.
